note: Saint Lucia, read on 2026-10-30 in the Revised Laws of Saint Lucia (2023) as the Attorney General's Chambers publishes them: the Immigration Act, section 12, and the Immigration (Permit Fees) Regulations (S.I. 117/2000), regulation 3 and its Schedule. Fees are in Eastern Caribbean dollars. An immigration officer may grant a permit to enter and remain for up to six months for, among other purposes, employment or trade or business (s. 12(1)); the Chief Immigration Officer may extend it to a year from entry (s. 12(3)); Cabinet may grant permission to remain for any period beyond a year, or permanent residence (s. 12(4)). The Regulations' Schedule, the fees for permits under section 12, gives a permit granting temporary resident at $1,000 and a permit granting permanent resident at $2,500 (written), extensions of stay at $100 per 21 days (not a residence route), and on every application stamp duty under the Stamp Duty Act and a non-refundable $50 application fee (not summed in). The temporary resident permit is taken to be Cabinet's permission beyond a year, which the Act names without that title; it serves any purpose, so it is `general`. Its term, renewal, decision time, the work it allows (the Labour Act's work permit is the work engine's), the years before permanent residence and where either is applied for aren't stated in what was read. OECS nationals' free movement isn't modelled here.

sources.title: Revised Laws of Saint Lucia (2023), Immigration Act, s. 12: permit to remain in the state
sources.said: may, at the request of the immigrant, grant him or her a permit to enter and remain in Saint Lucia for such period not exceeding 6 months as may be specified in the permit ... for purposes of employment; ... may from time to time extend the period specified in the permit up to a maximum of one year from the date of entry into Saint Lucia of the immigrant to whom the permit relates. ... (4) Cabinet may grant an immigrant — (a) permission to remain in the State for any period exceeding one year; or (b) permanent residence in the State.
